front_prompt: 4. Why do lines of latitude shrink in size toward the poles while meridians of longitude do not?
back_answer: Parallels of latitude are full circles drawn horizontally parallel to the Equator. Because the Earth is a sphere, the circumference of these horizontal cross-sections decreases from the Equator (largest circle) toward the poles, where they become single points (90° N/S). Meridians of longitude are vertical half-circles running from pole to pole; since all poles are at equal distances along the sphere, all meridians have equal length.
